title: Daily routine — the present tense
goal: Talk about what you do every day — and master the one part of Persian you truly have to memorize: the present stem of the verb.
bekal: build present-tense sentences with می + stem + ending
use the twenty most common everyday verbs

dialogs.title: گفتگو — یک روزِ معمولی
dialogs.intro: At the language institute's café. Maryam asks Budi about his daily routine in Tehran.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.id: In the morning I get up at six.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.id: That's early! Do you have breakfast?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: بله، نان و پنیر می‌خورم و چای می‌نوشم.
lines.baca: bale, nân o panir mikhoram va châi minusham.
lines.id: Yes, I eat bread and cheese and drink tea.
lines.literal: yes, bread and cheese eat-I and tea drink-I.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.id: What do you do after that?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: با مترو به شرکت می‌روم. ساعتِ هشت آنجا هستم.
lines.baca: bâ metro be sherkat miravam. sâ'at-e hasht ânjâ hastam.
lines.id: I go to the office by metro. By eight I'm there.
lines.literal: with metro to company go-I. hour-of eight there am-I.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: معمولاً در شرکت. گاهی با همکارانم بیرون می‌رویم.
lines.baca: ma'mulan dar sherkat. gâhi bâ hamkârânam birun miravim.
lines.id: Usually at the office. Sometimes we go out with my colleagues.
lines.literal: usually in company. sometimes with colleagues-my out go-we.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.id: What do you do in the evenings?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: فارسی می‌خوانم. هر شب یک ساعت درس می‌خوانم.
lines.baca: fârsi mikhânam. har shab yek sâ'at dars mikhânam.
lines.id: I study Persian. Every night I study for an hour.
lines.literal: Persian read-I. every night one hour lesson read-I.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.id: Well done! Do you watch TV too?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: کم. ولی هر روز خبر گوش می‌دهم.
lines.baca: kam. vali har ruz khabar gush midaham.
lines.id: A little. But every day I listen to the news.
lines.literal: little. but every day news ear give-I.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.id: When do you go to bed?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: حدودِ یازده. آخرِ هفته دیرتر می‌خوابم.
lines.baca: hodud-e yâzdah. âkhar-e hafte dirtar mikhâbam.
lines.id: Around eleven. On weekends I go to bed later.
lines.literal: around-of eleven. end-of week later sleep-I.

notes: ⚠️ **The present stem can't be guessed from the infinitive, and it is the one thing in Persian you truly have to memorize.** رفتن ("go") has the stem **رو**, دیدن ("see") has **بین**, خواستن ("want") has **خواه**. No rule will help you; there is only a list. The full list is at the back of this book, and it's the page you'll open most over the next six months.

**The good news: you've had the endings since unit 1.** ـم، ـی، ـد، ـیم، ـید، ـند — the same six endings for every Persian verb, without a single exception. Compare French or Spanish, with three sets of endings plus irregular verbs.

⚠️ **The prefix بر goes in front of می, not after it.** برگشتن ("return") becomes **برمی‌گردم** (*barmigardam*), not می‌برگردم. There aren't many prefixed verbs like this — برگشتن، برداشتن، بازکردن — but all three are common.

***Âfarin!*** **(آفرین) = "well done! bravo!"** The praise you'll hear most from teachers, parents, and anyone pleased with your effort. A native Persian word, and one that will often come your way when you try to speak.

***Âdam-e monazzami hastid*** (آدمِ منظمی هستید) uses the little ـی ending from unit 3 again: "an organized person". آدم is literally "Adam" and means "person, human being" — much like English "a son of Adam".

**Spoken Tehrani shortens almost everything:** می‌روم → **می‌رم** (*miram*), می‌خورم → **می‌خورم** (unchanged), می‌گویم → **می‌گم** (*migam*), می‌شوم → **می‌شم** (*misham*), می‌خواهم → **می‌خوام** (*mikhâm*), می‌دهم → **می‌دم** (*midam*). Four of the six most frequent verbs get shorter — that's why unit 14 exists.

grammars.title: The formula: می + present stem + ending
body: The complete formula for the Persian present tense. Take the present stem from the list, put می in front and the person ending at the back. Here it is with رفتن ("go"), whose stem is رو:
after: **The negative: swap می for نمی.** می‌روم → نمی‌روم (*nemiravam*). Note the sound: **ne-mi-**, not *na-mi-*.
⚠️ **Two verbs never take می in the present:** داشتن (دارم، داری، دارد …) and بودن (هستم، هستی، هست …). You met both in units 1 and 4.
If the stem ends in a vowel, a linking ی is added: گفتن has the stem **گو**, so می‌گویم (*miguyam*), می‌گویی، می‌گوید. Likewise شدن, stem **شو** → می‌شوم.

grammars.title: Twenty everyday verbs
after: The ten most common combinations: **کار می‌کنم** (I work), **زندگی می‌کنم** (I live), **صحبت می‌کنم** (I speak), **فکر می‌کنم** (I think), **تماشا می‌کنم** (I watch), **گوش می‌دهم** (I listen), **بیدار می‌شوم** (I wake up), **خسته می‌شوم** (I get tired), **دوست دارم** (I like), **درس می‌خوانم** (I study).
⚠️ Note that **خواندن** means "read", "study", **and** "sing" all at once. درس می‌خوانم = "I study", آواز می‌خوانم = "I sing", کتاب می‌خوانم = "I read a book". Context always tells them apart.

grammars.title: How often
after: ⚠️ **The words هرگز and هیچ‌وقت demand a negative verb**, just like "at all" in unit 2: هیچ‌وقت سیگار **نمی‌کشم** ("I never smoke", literally "never I don't smoke"). Leaving out نمی is a mistake.
These words usually go **in front of the verb**, but Persian is flexible: من همیشه صبح ورزش می‌کنم and همیشه من صبح ورزش می‌کنم are both correct.

sections.title: A day from morning to night

blocks.text: Three meals: **صبحانه** (*sobhâne*, breakfast), **ناهار** (*nâhâr*, lunch), **شام** (*shâm*, dinner). All of them take the verb خوردن ("eat") — there's no special verb for each.

blocks.title: An Iranian breakfast, and why you'll love it
items: An Iranian breakfast is نان و پنیر (bread and white cheese), plus one of مربا (jam), عسل (honey), کره (butter), خامه (clotted cream), or گردو (walnuts) — and always چای.

There are hot breakfasts too: کله‌پاچه (sheep's head and trotters soup, eaten at dawn and not for everyone) and حلیم (wheat porridge with meat, sweet and filling). You may know حلیم as *haleem* from South Asian cooking — the same word, and a very similar dish.

blocks.title: Four sentences to describe your day
items: "In the morning I get up at ..." — صبح ساعتِ ... بیدار می‌شوم.
"I go to work by ..." — با ... سرِکار می‌روم.
"I usually have lunch at ..." — معمولاً ناهار را در ... می‌خورم.
"Every night I study Persian for an hour." — هر شب یک ساعت فارسی می‌خوانم. Say this last one to an Iranian and the answer will almost certainly be آفرین.
I go to the office by metro.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the correct present-tense form.
Put the words in the right order.

answers: من ساعتِ شش بیدار می‌شوم. — با مترو به شرکت می‌روم. — هر شب فارسی می‌خوانم. — تلویزیون تماشا نمی‌کنم. — ناهار کجا می‌خورید؟
صبح ساعتِ شش بیدار می‌شوم. — با مترو به شرکت می‌روم. — هر شب فارسی می‌خوانم. — من تلویزیون تماشا نمی‌کنم. — ناهار کجا می‌خورید؟
